description:
The proof sketch (64fd3afd) proves the run-length characterisation behind `BchDistanceBound::minimum_distance_lower_bound`, but the classical Vandermonde argument connecting the witnessed consecutive-root run to an actual minimum-distance lower bound is named by no issue. This follow-up owns that Lean obligation: the BCH-bound theorem (a codeword with fewer than delta nonzero coordinates vanishing on delta-1 consecutive roots is zero, via Vandermonde nonsingularity), bound to the production surface per the sketch's model-plus-refinement conventions.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A Lean proof of the classical BCH bound ties the witnessed run to the minimum-distance claim of the public API, following the proof sketch's binding conventions, and passes the repository proof gates.
- [hard] REQ-02: The sketch's assumptions register is extended or discharged accordingly; no untracked assumption.
title: Prove the Vandermonde step: witnessed BCH bound implies the minimum-distance claim
